P.02 — YOUR IPHONE IS ALREADY A SERIOUS CAMERA
01  —  The Camera You Own
The iPhone Creator Guide
Shot OniPhone
01  /  Start Here
Your iPhone Is Already
A Serious Camera
It shoots 4K. It has three focal lengths, a log profile, and a sensor that holds up anywhere the light is decent.

That is more camera than most of the content you are making actually needs. When footage looks amateur, the body is almost never the reason.

It is the light you did not move, the frame you did not think about, the audio you recorded from six feet away, and the settings you never opened.

Fix those four and the same phone produces work people assume was shot on a cinema camera.

M02.1
Photo Stephen shooting handheld on iPhone Portrait 268 × 346 · 3:4
Waist-up · phone visible in frame
What Actually Changes How The Shot Reads
My ranking · not a measurement
Lighting Move one lamp, or turn to face the window.
Framing & angle Lens height, distance, and what sits behind you.
Audio People forgive a soft image. They leave on bad sound.
Settings Set once, stop thinking about it. Page 03.
Movement Slow and deliberate, or locked off. Nothing in between.
The camera body Last on the list, and the one everyone tries to buy first.
Where The Phone Wins
iPhone
Always with you. Sets up in seconds. Shoots, edits and posts on one device. Good enough that the audience never asks what you used.
Where The Body Wins
Dedicated Camera
Low light, long lenses, shallow depth, and long-form work. Real advantages. None of them are what is holding your content back today.

Which Lens To Reach For
Lock it before you record
1×Main · Default
Best sensor and best low light. Shoot here unless you have a reason not to.
0.5×Ultra Wide
Tight rooms and establishing shots. Keep faces out of the corners.
2–5×Telephoto
Flattering for talking head, and it separates you from the room. Needs light.
From Stephen
Tap your face to set focus and exposure, then press and hold until it locks. Do this before every take and the footage stops shifting brightness mid-sentence.

P.04 — NATIVE CAMERA VS BLACKMAGIC CAMERA · split
03  —  Two Apps
The iPhone Creator Guide
AppNative / BMD
03  /  Which App
Native Camera
Or Blackmagic
Both live on the same phone and use the same sensor. The difference is how much the app decides for you.
M04.1
Screenshot Native Camera, video mode 9:16 UI, letterboxed into 328 × 214
Show 4K/30 badge + exposure lock
Option 01
Native Camera
The phone makes the calls. You get a very good image with almost no decisions, and you are recording two seconds after you pick it up.
Reach For It When
Something is happening now and you have one chance at it
You are shooting handheld B-roll on the move
The clip is going straight out with light editing
You want Cinematic or Action mode
M04.2
Screenshot Blackmagic Camera, recording UI 16:9 landscape UI · 328 × 214
Show ISO, shutter, WB, Apple Log
Option 02
Blackmagic Camera
You make the calls. Shutter, ISO, white balance and codec are all yours, and the app stops quietly changing things between takes.
Reach For It When
You are shooting a talking head you will grade
The light is mixed, tricky, or changing
You need shots to match across a whole shoot
You want Apple Log, or to record to an SSD
The Honest Answer
I use both, most weeks. Native for anything spontaneous, Blackmagic for anything I have set up for. If you are new to this, shoot native until your lighting and framing are consistent. Manual control on top of bad light just gets you a well-exposed bad shot.

P.05 — APPLE LOG + THE CINEMATIC LOOK · three-stage comparison
04  —  Apple Log
The iPhone Creator Guide
Apple Log1/48ISO 55
04  /  Log & Colour
Apple Log And
The Cinematic Look
Log is a flat, low-contrast recording that keeps detail in the brightest and darkest parts of the shot so you can decide how it looks later.
M05.1
Video Frame Apple Log, straight off the phone 16:9 · 202 × 236 crop
Flat, grey, low contrast
01   Flat Original
Looks broken. It is not. Every highlight and shadow is still there, waiting.
→
M05.2
Video Frame Same frame, corrected 16:9 · 202 × 236 crop
LUT applied, exposure + WB fixed
02   Corrected
Conversion LUT on, exposure and white balance set. Neutral and accurate.
→
M05.3
Video Frame Same frame, final grade 16:9 · 202 × 236 crop
The look that ships
03   Final Grade
Now it is a choice. Warmth, contrast and colour pushed on purpose.
Step 01
Log
Record flat in Blackmagic
Step 02
Convert
Apple Log to Rec.709 LUT
Step 03
Correct
Exposure, white balance, contrast
Step 04
Create
Then, and only then, the look
Shutter, Without The Theory
24fps ×2 1/48 The film look. My default.
30fps ×2 1/60 Standard for social.
60fps ×2 1/120 Only when you will slow it down.
Double the frame rate. That is the whole rule. Faster looks choppy, slower turns to mush.
Two Things Log Will Not Forgive
Exposure
Expose slightly brighter than looks right on screen, but never let the highlights clip. Use false colour or zebras. Underexposed Log turns to noise the moment you grade it.
White Balance
Set it by hand and lock it. Auto drifts between takes, and matching shots that each drifted differently is the worst job in the edit.
If you are not going to grade it, do not shoot it. Log straight to the feed looks worse than native.

P.06 — SHOOT WITH INTENTION · contact sheet
05  —  Coverage
The iPhone Creator Guide
Coverage6 Shots
05  /  Coverage
Shoot With Intention
Knowing the settings is the easy half. The creators whose work looks finished are thinking in shots, not clips.
Wide → Medium → Close → Detail → Movement → Reveal One subject · six ways
M06.1
Video FrameWide16:9 · 213 × 176
Full room, subject small
01Wide
Where are we. Opens the piece and gives everything after it a place to happen.
M06.2
Video FrameMedium16:9 · 213 × 176
Waist up, eye level
02Medium
Your default. Most of what you say to camera lives here. Conversational, not formal.
M06.3
Video FrameClose16:9 · 213 × 176
Chest up, tighter
03Close
Save it for the line that matters. Used constantly it stops meaning anything.
M06.4
Video FrameDetail16:9 · 213 × 176
Hands, product, screen
04Detail
The shot that saves edits. Cuts over any mistake and proves you were actually there.
M06.5
Video FrameMovement16:9 · 213 × 176
Mid push-in or pan
05Movement
Slow push, slow pan, or walk with the subject. Start moving before you record.
M06.6
Video FrameReveal16:9 · 213 × 176
End of the move
06Reveal
Start hidden, end on the thing. Behind a door, past a shoulder, up from a table.
Shoot All Six
Of the same subject, in the same light, before you move on. It takes four extra minutes.
Hold Longer
Ten seconds per shot, minimum. Short clips are the reason edits feel rushed.
Vary The Height
Six shots from one tripod height is still one angle. Move the camera, not just the zoom.

P.07 — LIGHTING + AUDIO · horizontal split
06  —  Light + Sound
The iPhone Creator Guide
Light+ Sound
06  /  The Two Fixes
Lighting And Audio
Nothing else on this list changes an iPhone image as fast, and both are mostly free.
Light
Direction beats brightness
M07.1
PhotoWindow light, 45°16:9 · 213 × 152
Same subject as M07.2
Good
Face the window, then turn about 45 degrees off it. Soft, directional, shows shape.
M07.2
PhotoOverhead ceiling light16:9 · 213 × 152
Same subject as M07.1
Bad
A ceiling light directly above you digs shadows into your eyes. Turn it off.
Where To Put It
One source, off to one side, higher than your eyeline. That is the whole setup.
Sound
Distance beats every microphone
M07.3
PhotoWireless lav clipped for a talking head16:9 · 328 × 236 · close crop
Show mic placement on the shirt
A cheap microphone six inches from your mouth beats an expensive one across the room. Clip it a hand's width below your chin, slightly off centre so your collar does not brush it.
Kill The Room First
Close the windows, turn off the fan and the fridge, and get off the hard floor. Echo cannot be removed later, only hidden.
Record A Safety
Let the phone mic run alongside the lav. It has saved more of my shoots than any other habit.
Listen Back Before You Move
Ten seconds on headphones. Cheaper than reshooting the whole thing tomorrow.
Phone Mic Is Fine
Outdoors with no wind, in a quiet room, within about two feet of your face, or on B-roll where the audio gets replaced anyway. Anywhere else, clip something on.

07  —  The Rig
The iPhone Creator Guide
Kit3 Tiers
07  /  Kit
Build Your
iPhone Creator Rig
In the order that actually helps. Most people buy tier three first and still have the problems tier one solves.
M08.1
Photo · Flat Lay The full iPhone creator rig, laid out Landscape 672 × 214 · 3.1:1 · overhead
Everything on this page, evenly spaced, single surface
Neutral background · soft even light · no props
Tier 01
Start Here
Fixes the two problems every beginner actually has: shake and sound.
Support
Tripod + phone clamp
Anything that holds still beats holding your arm out.
Audio
Wired lav mic
Plugs into USB-C. Cheapest real upgrade on this page.
Light
A window
Free, and better than most panels people buy first.
Storage
Space on the phone
4K/60 fills a phone fast. Clear it before, not during.
Tier 02
Level Up
Where the work starts looking deliberate instead of merely tidy.
Audio
Wireless lav kit
Two transmitters, one receiver. You stop being tethered.
Light
One LED panel + diffusion
Bi-colour, battery powered, softbox on the front.
Optics
Variable ND filter
Holds your shutter outdoors instead of forcing it faster.
Support
Mini tripod / desk stand
Overheads, product shots, anything at arm's length.
Tier 03
Full Creator Rig
Built to shoot all day without thinking about the gear once.
Body
Cage + side handle
Mounting points for mic, light and monitor. Runs cooler.
Motion
Gimbal
Movement that holds. Slower and smoother than your hands.
Storage
External SSD
Record straight out of Blackmagic. No transfer afterwards.
Light
Second light or bounce
Separates you from the background, or fills the shadow side.
Buy In Order
Finish a tier before you start the next one. A gimbal will not fix bad audio, and a cage will not fix a shot lit from the ceiling. Every tier here costs less than the camera body people think they need.

P.09 — MY IPHONE CONTENT WORKFLOW · infographic
08  —  Workflow
The iPhone Creator Guide
Pipeline10 Steps
08  /  Workflow
From Idea
To Published
The same ten steps every time. The order is what keeps a shoot from turning into a salvage job in the edit.
Capture  ·  On The Day
Steps 01–05
01
Idea
One sentence. What is this video actually for.
02
Settings
Preset from page 03. Lock focus, exposure, white balance.
03
A-Roll
Everything you say. Medium first, close on the lines that matter.
04
B-Roll
All six shots, before you break the setup down.
05
Transfer
Off the phone the same day. Dated folder, named properly.
Finish  ·  At The Desk
Steps 06–10
06
Edit
Cut the A-roll first. Nothing else until the words work.
07
Colour
Convert Log, correct, then grade. In that order.
08
Audio
Levels matched, room noise down, music under the voice.
09
Export
H.264, at the frame rate you shot. Do not re-time it.
10
Publish
Caption, cover frame, out. Keep the project file.

Same Day
Transfer before you sleep. Footage left on a phone is footage you will not use.
Words First
No B-roll, music or colour until the A-roll cut holds on its own.
One Folder
Project, footage, exports, together. Future you will need the file again.
